vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 45339 / ARVO arvo:45339 / libxml2 xmlParseReference bad-free

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this composite workspace. The metadata repo and saved `patch.diff` are libxslt-side, but the crashing source lines are in the bundled libxml2 checkout at `7d02c7291f5c0ba56b9d8c04af7690cf11e47f07`.

classification.classification_note: The saved ASan symptom is an invalid free in `xmlFreeNodeList`. Source inspection shows the freed pointer falls inside the parser-dictionary pool allocated by `xmlDictAddString`, but the node carrying that name sits on a reused `SAX_COMPAT_MODE` document whose `doc->dict` is NULL, so `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` misclassifies dict-backed storage as heap-owned.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` while libxslt's `xslt` fuzz target parsed the staged malformed stylesheet through `xmlReadMemory()`. The witness begins with an invalid XML declaration (`version="0.0"`) and then malformed internal-subset `laugh*` entity declarations, so fatal parser-error helpers set `ctxt->wellFormed = 0` and `ctxt->disableSAX = 1`. Because `xmlParseDocument()` calls `startDocument` only when `!ctxt->disableSAX`, the normal SAX2 document setup is skipped; later `xmlParseEntityDecl()` therefore enters its SAX-compatibility fallback and creates or preserves `ctxt->myDoc` without assigning `myDoc->dict`. In the vulnerable staged libxml2 checkout `7d02c7291f5c0ba56b9d8c04af7690cf11e47f07`, `xmlParseReference()` then resolves a later general-entity reference and, without the later-restored `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;`, reparses attacker-defined replacement text through `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal()`. That nested parser shares the outer parser dictionary and `dictNames` but reuses the existing `myDoc`, so it materializes nodes whose `name` pointers come from the parser dictionary while `cur->doc->dict` remains NULL. When the nested `laugh*` expansion trips `xmlParserEntityCheck()`, `xmlParseReference()` cleans up the returned list with `xmlFreeNodeList(list)`. `xmlFreeNodeList()` loads `dict = cur->doc->dict` as NULL and then `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` calls `xmlFree()` on parser-dictionary storage; ASan reports the freed address `0x6190000006c0` is 320 bytes inside the 1048-byte region allocated by `xmlDictAddString()`. The direct source-side fix visible in the staged libxml2 history is commit `968495442964f3ea72499dfbdba9e2fa9d77f9b7`, which restores `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` immediately after `xmlParseEntityRef()`.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled stylesheet bytes and hands them to libxml2's document parser.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the malformed XML/XSLT text saved in `gt_results/arvo_45339/poc`, including `<?xml version="0.0"?>`, malformed internal-subset `laugh*` entity declarations, and later `&laugh30;` / `&laugh14;` references that reach the vulnerable parser path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After reading a later entity reference, the vulnerable function returns only when `ent == NULL`; it omits the needed `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` guard that was later restored in staged libxml2 commit `96849544`. That omission lets entity reparsing continue even though earlier fatal errors already suppressed normal `startDocument` setup and later DTD handling left the reused compatibility document without `doc->dict`.
root_cause.note: The local staged libxml2 history contains the direct two-line revert fix, while the saved result-dir `patch.diff` is only the top-level libxslt-side cleanup commit.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `xmlFreeNodeList()` decides string ownership from `cur->doc->dict`; on the crashing path that document dictionary is NULL, so the function frees a parser-dictionary node name as if it were heap-owned.
sink.note: ASan reports the freed address `0x6190000006c0` as 320 bytes inside the 1048-byte region `[0x619000000580,0x619000000998)` allocated by `xmlDictAddString`, and steps 4, 8, 13 show why `cur->doc->dict` is NULL at this point.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-defined internal-entity replacement text is reconsumed here. The callee reparses it into a temporary node list while sharing the outer parser dictionary and reusing the outer compatibility document.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged witness defines a nested `laugh*` entity chain and later references it from the document body/attribute content; this call reparses that replacement text after `xmlParseEntityRef()` resolves the referenced entity.

parser_admitted.description: The stylesheet survives initial document setup far enough to enter element-content parsing and dispatch a later `&...;` token into `xmlParseReference()`, the direct caller of the crashing `xmlFreeNodeList` frame.

coarse_trace.summary: The libxslt fuzz target feeds the staged malformed stylesheet directly into libxml2; the leading invalid XML declaration makes the outer parser not well formed and disables SAX before `xmlParseDocument()` reaches `startDocument`.

Because `startDocument` is skipped, `ctxt->myDoc` stays NULL until malformed internal entity declarations force the SAX-compatibility document path, creating or preserving a document whose `dict` stays NULL; a later entity reference then reaches `xmlParseReference()` without the restored `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;`.

Balanced-chunk reparsing shares the parser dictionary but reuses that NULL-dict document, creating nodes whose names point into dict storage; `xmlParserEntityCheck()` frees the list and `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` triggers the saved invalid free.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact staged stylesheet bytes are handed unchanged to libxml2 for document parsing; the `0` options leave `XML_PARSE_NODICT` unset, so parser contexts keep dictionary-backed names enabled.

The leading `<?xml version="0.0"?>` already routes this non-recovery parse through fatal parser-error helpers before `xmlParseDocument()` reaches `startDocument`. That transition leaves the outer parse not well formed and disables SAX; later malformed DTD bytes keep the same fatal state.

Because step 2 set `ctxt->disableSAX != 0`, this guarded callback does not run before DTD parsing begins. `ctxt->myDoc` therefore stays NULL instead of following `xmlSAX2StartDocument()`'s normal path that creates the document and assigns `doc->dict = ctxt->dict` when dictionary names are enabled.

While malformed internal general-entity declarations from the same DTD are parsed, the SAX-compatibility branch fires because step 3 left `ctxt->myDoc == NULL`; later malformed declarations can preserve the same document because its version is `SAX_COMPAT_MODE`. `xmlNewDoc()` zero-initializes the document structure, and this block never assigns `doc->dict`, so the outer parser now carries entity declarations on a compatibility document whose dictionary field remains NULL.

depends_on.via: ctxt->myDoc == NULL makes the SAX_COMPAT_MODE branch true

fine_trace.note: A later general-entity reference from the same stylesheet resolves to non-NULL `ent`. Vulnerable libxml2 continues past this point even though step 2 already set `ctxt->wellFormed = 0`; the later fix re-adds `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` between the second and third lines here.
Because this is the first parse of that internal entity on the witnessed path, `xmlParseReference()` reparses the attacker-defined replacement text into temporary list `list`.

The fresh balanced-chunk parser drops its own dictionary and reuses the outer parser dictionary. Because step 1 passed option `0`, the outer parser kept `dictNames = 1`, and this function later copies that flag too (`ctxt->dictNames = oldctxt->dictNames`), so nested SAX2 element creation keeps using parser-dictionary names.

Instead of creating a fresh document with `newDoc->dict = ctxt->dict`, the nested parser reuses the outer `myDoc`. From step 4 onward that document is the SAX-compatibility document with `doc->dict == NULL`, so the nested parse inherits a document object that does not advertise ownership of parser-dictionary strings.

When the nested entity text reaches the malformed `<x:copy>` token with an undefined prefix, SAX2 builds the full QName in the shared parser dictionary and rebinds `localname` to that dict-backed string.

The nested parse materializes an element node under the reused document from step 8. `xmlNewDocNodeEatName()` passes that pointer through to `xmlNewNodeEatName()`, which stores `cur->name = name` without copying, so the new node keeps a dict-backed `ret->name` while `ret->doc->dict` is still NULL.

The nested parser returns the newly built node list to `xmlParseReference()`. This assignment is guarded by `if ((lst != NULL) && (ret == XML_ERR_OK))`, so a non-NULL `list` at the caller implies the balanced-chunk parse succeeded and handed back these reused-document nodes.

The staged witness's nested `laugh*` expansion trips libxml2's entity-abuse cleanup. Because step 11 produced non-NULL `list` only on `ret == XML_ERR_OK`, and `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)` left `XML_PARSE_NOENT` unset, the later `xmlFreeNodeList(list)` arms in `xmlParseReference()` are excluded; the unsymbolized caller frame is this `xmlParserEntityCheck()` cleanup branch.

On the first node passed from step 12, this loads `dict` from the reused SAX-compatibility document. That document still has `doc->dict == NULL`, so `xmlFreeNodeList()` loses the ownership information for the dict-backed `cur->name` pointer.

Sink. With `dict == NULL`, `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` falls through to `xmlFree(cur->name)`, even though the saved ASan allocation stack places that pointer inside the parser-dictionary pool allocated by `xmlDictAddString` at `libxml2/dict.c:266`.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The saved result-dir `patch.diff` is libxslt commit `22f12ce58eb5f41d23bb205530034b29aac03700`, which removes direct `xmlXPathInit()` / `xmlInitMemory()` calls but does not touch the crashing libxml2 parser/tree code.

direct_fix_in_staged_libxml2_history.change: Re-adds `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` immediately after `ent = xmlParseEntityRef(ctxt);` in `xmlParseReference()`.

evidence_note: The saved ASan stack identifies `xmlFreeNodeList -> xmlParseReference -> xmlParseContentInternal`, but frame 2 has no source line in `sanitizer_trace.txt` or `default_crash_trace.txt`. This GT therefore keeps `sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_stack[2].line` unsymbolized and uses source semantics to choose `xmlParseReference()`'s `xmlParserEntityCheck()` cleanup arm: `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal()` initializes `*lst = NULL` and only returns non-NULL `list` on `ret == XML_ERR_OK` (`parser.c:13312`, `parser.c:13411-13420`), `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)` leaves `XML_PARSE_NOENT` unset, and those facts exclude the later `xmlFreeNodeList(list)` arms while leaving the 7212-7214 branch as the reachable handoff into `tree.c:3750`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image. The saved result-dir `patch.diff` is libxslt-side and does not touch the crashing libxml2 path; the direct source-side fix visible in the staged libxml2 history is commit `968495442964f3ea72499dfbdba9e2fa9d77f9b7` restoring `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The missing `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` guard lets libxml2 reparse entity text after fatal errors into nodes whose names are interned in the shared parser dictionary but attached to a reused `myDoc` with `doc->dict == NULL`; that ownership mismatch is exactly what makes `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` free storage from the ASan allocation pool.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `xmlFreeNodeList -> xmlParseReference -> xmlParseContentInternal`, but the `xmlParseReference` line is unsymbolized in the saved sanitizer text. Fine-trace steps 12-14 place that frame at the `xmlParserEntityCheck()` cleanup arm using source semantics (`list != NULL` only after successful balanced-chunk parse, and `XML_PARSE_NOENT` is unset at `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)`), then carry control into the exact sink at `tree.c:3750`.

format.contract: Exactly the staged stylesheet text saved in `gt_results/arvo_45339/poc`: it begins with `<?xml version="0.0"?>`, contains malformed internal-subset `laugh*` entity declarations, and later includes `&laugh30;` / `&laugh14;` references.
